title: Application-Driven Exascale: The JUPITER Benchmark Suite
problem: Synthetic benchmarks alone inadequately represent real user application requirements for HPC system design and procurement. Exascale supercomputers require application-driven benchmarking to ensure system utility and guide procurement decisions.
motivation: With substantial investments in leadership-class exascale supercomputers, procurement and system design decisions must be informed by realistic application performance requirements aligned with open science principles.
method: The benchmark suite collects 16 real scientific applications—programs that researchers use in climate modeling, physics simulations, and other fields—to understand what computing power and features an exascale supercomputer actually needs. It identifies specific hardware and software requirements, documents each application's behavior and how it performs as you add more processors (called scaling), and releases the complete suite as open-source software so any institution can use and verify the results.
key_novelty: Unlike artificial test programs, this suite uses 16 real scientific applications to define what an exascale supercomputer must do, and this approach was proven by guiding the actual procurement of Europe's first exascale computer.
contributions: JUPITER Benchmark Suite with 16 real applications from diverse scientific domains
Infrastructure and methodology for application-driven exascale system procurement
Scalability studies and performance characterization of real HPC applications
Open source release enabling reproducibility and widespread community adoption

metrics.speedup: application scaling efficiency through scalability studies

limitations: Limitations and methodological constraints are not explicitly discussed in the work.
primary_theme: Benchmarking suite for exascale HPC system procurement
